newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower on dollar short covering.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower on dollar short covering.

text.p: The won closed Friday's trading weaker due to dollar short covering and the U.S. unit's strength against the Japnese yen in the Tokyo market, traders said.
They added there was active dollar buying by foreign stock market investors who felt the won had strengthened enough to convert their bourse earnings.
The won closed at 857.10, compared to Thursday's close of 854.90. The unit opened trading at a high of 854.00 and touched a low of 857.30.
Dollar selling intervention by the central bank at the 857.00 level had little impact on trading, dealers said.
"Next week, I see the dollar continue to strengthen slowly, starting at around 857 and rising," said a European bank dealer.
Friday saw the first decline in the won since a central bank official earlier this week said the bank would actively try to stabilise the domestic currency's fall.
The central bank has refused to confirm or deny talk of its intervention in the interbank market.
Monday's base mid-rate was pegged at 856.70, against Friday's 855.50.
